title: Episode 522: What Was Your Eureka Moment with AI? Smarter Workflows for BC Development

chapters.title: Introduction and BC Tech Days discussion
Guest introduction - Tom, MVP, and developer tooling focus
AI model improvements and benchmarking challenges
Fable model safeguards and fallback mechanisms
AL language knowledge gaps in AI models
Measuring model awareness of AL syntax and features
Using multiple AI models for different development tasks
Cost optimization and workflow automation with agents
Advisory models and Claude Code features for development
Setting up agentic workflows and MCP servers for developers
Creating custom MCP servers for debugging and AI as co-founder
Rethinking software development value and problem-solving paradigm
Gotchas in AI-assisted AL development and shift to test verification

features.name: Central gauge benchmarking tool
features.description: A tool that measures and benchmarks all AI models for AL development tasks. Tom has found that models are now so good at AL tasks that the test set is saturated with near-perfect results, requiring new creative testing approaches.
caveats: Test set is saturated - models perform too well on existing tests
New metrics and test approaches are needed to differentiate model performance

features.name: Fable model with safeguard fallback
features.description: Fable AI model includes safeguards that trigger on AL tasks, refusing to work on certain tasks. The model can fall back to Opus or other models when safeguards are triggered, making it harder to benchmark actual Fable performance.
caveats: Safeguards can block legitimate AL testing tasks
Fallback behavior makes true model capability assessment difficult
Models may have automatic mode for selecting which model to use for different task types

features.name: Microsoft AL harness for model evaluation
features.description: Microsoft provides a harness framework for evaluating AI models on AL development tasks. Tom is working with the Microsoft creator of this tool and creating his own fork to test additional metrics beyond what Microsoft currently supports.
caveats: Microsoft does not currently accept pull requests on their repository
Custom fork being developed to add extra metrics

features.name: AL language syntax knowledge gaps in AI models
features.description: GPT models have documented issues with understanding AL language concepts, particularly interfaces. Models trained on different languages like TypeScript can create code but do not understand AL-specific syntax and format requirements.
caveats: Models trained on older AL syntax versions don't know newer features
AL is a younger language with more frequent changes than C, TypeScript, or Python

features.name: Model-agnostic baseline augmentation through guidelines
features.description: Custom guideline files can be created and added to prompt instructions via markdown files to raise all models to the same baseline knowledge level by teaching them about AL concepts they lack in their training data.
caveats: Requires manual identification of knowledge gaps through benchmarking
Guideline files may not be fully public

features.name: Subsection-based model capability reporting
features.description: Benchmarking data divided into subsections by AL concept including interfaces, tables, records, field reports to help developers understand which AL language features a model is aware of and where additional context needs to be provided.
caveats: Information is available but not immediately prominent on Tom's site
Requires users to know what to look for
test data is public on GitHub so could influence future model training

features.name: Advisory model selection in Claude Code
features.description: Feature to set an advisory model like Fable in Claude Code that the main model can consult for additional perspective and feedback during development tasks.

features.name: Multi-model workflow orchestration
features.description: Ability to route different development tasks to different AI models based on their strengths - using Opus for planning, Fable for review, Sonnet for coding to optimize cost and performance. Demonstrated through a pipeline with 13 stages.
caveats: workflow is ISV-specific and may not work for partners or VS Code users

features.name: PAL MCP for consensus feedback
features.description: MCP server called PAL that adds other AI providers like OpenAI GPT-5.5 Pro and Gemini 3.1 Pro preview for cross-model consensus and additional feedback during development tasks.

features.name: Automatic code compilation and testing in agentic workflows
features.description: Agentic workflow capability where AI automatically compiles, deploys, runs tests, detects failures, fixes them and re-tests iteratively without manual intervention.

features.name: AL MCP server integration with Claude
features.description: MCP server for AL that Claude can use to execute AL-specific tasks including publishing to sandbox, running tests, analyzing source code with source code analyzers, and fixing compilation errors.

features.name: Simplified MCP server setup via AI
features.description: Users can provide an MCP server GitHub repo to Claude and ask it to set up the server without needing to understand JSON format or configuration details.

features.name: Custom MCP for BC performance and debugging
features.description: Developer created custom MCP server for instrumental profiling analysis and performance debugging of Business Central, including converter for MTC files to Firefox profiler format without dependency on Microsoft files.
caveats: Created by developer, not a standard tool

features.name: AI-assisted driver development
features.description: Developer used Claude with access to GitHub and Wireshark to create a Linux kernel driver for fingerprint sensor by recording Windows traffic and analyzing encryption patterns, completed in approximately 8 hours.
caveats: Demonstrates capability but outside Business Central scope

features.name: Test-first code verification approach
features.description: Developer reports spending more time reviewing tests than code, focusing on scenario validation rather than code inspection. As long as tests pass and no performance regression, code quality is acceptable.
caveats: Applies mainly to automated and simpler tasks, not new features

features.name: Future AI-native development without language visibility
features.description: Speculation that future development will operate at higher abstraction where developers work only with questions and answers, letting AI create executable code without human visibility into the language used.
features.status_evidence_quote: I can't see why not. It's still going to be for the next foreseeable future. We will still look at the inner workings of
caveats: Speculative vision
May still require visibility for regulatory or concurrent posting requirements

features.name: AI abstraction layer for financial postings
features.description: Discussion of how AI could abstract away code inspection for regulatory compliance, while still ensuring regulatory requirements like concurrent postings and number series handling are maintained through tests rather than manual code review.
caveats: regulatory compliance still required
testing still needed

features.name: Multi-model AI orchestration workflow
features.description: Strategy to use different AI models for different tasks - using larger models for spec creation and review, while offloading coding tasks to cheaper open-source or local models to minimize token costs.
caveats: hypothetical workflow
requires manual implementation
depends on model availability

features.name: Open-source model evaluation for AL coding
features.description: Testing of open-source models like GLM and Llama for AL code generation as potential replacements for commercial models. Plans to add local models and open-router options to a website for performance and cost comparison.
caveats: not yet tested in real AL programming
only small tests conducted
reasoning tasks still require different models

features.name: Local model hosting for reduced token costs
features.description: Discussion of using local models on hardware to reduce ongoing API token costs, even if processing takes longer, particularly for background tasks like CI/CD pipelines that do not require immediate results.
caveats: requires hardware investment
processing time increases
not suitable for real-time tasks

features.name: Per-use pricing for GitHub Copilot and AI services
features.description: Reference to Microsoft moving to per-use billing model for GitHub Copilot, with prediction that other AI providers including Anthropic will follow suit after going public.
caveats: prediction based on market trends
timing uncertain

features.name: AI model harness for workflow management
features.description: Concept of a unified harness to manage and orchestrate multiple AI models, controlling how data flows between them, handling input/output, and processing. Could be self-hosted locally to avoid recurring API costs.
caveats: not yet implemented
requires development effort
different use cases may have different requirements

features.name: Local open source AI models
features.description: Discussion of local open source models getting more attention for specific tasks, with potential cost savings through local hardware versus paid cloud subscriptions.
features.status_evidence_quote: my prediction for 2027 will be you'll see a lot of these local models getting or these open source local models getting a little
caveats: Prediction for future adoption
Effectiveness depends on local harness implementation

features.name: Fable AI
features.description: A new AI tool that was rapidly benchmarked after release. Had usage limits and rate resets, with updates to availability extended to July 12th.
features.status_evidence_quote: I think I had the benchmark ready like an hour after Fable was released
caveats: Has usage limits per account
Resets on schedule
Availability extended through July 12th
